Daily Digest · Computer Science

Vision Models Learn to See Longer, Reason Deeper

Today's papers reveal a maturing ecosystem where multimodal systems tackle increasingly complex spatial and temporal reasoning. From efficient view synthesis that bakes cross-view information into lightweight MLPs, to foundation models that now ground themselves in precise depth and geometry, the field is moving beyond pretrained backbones toward tightly integrated perception pipelines. The surprising throughline: constraint breeds innovation—whether it's parameter efficiency in clinical LLMs or efficient rendering without 3D reconstruction, researchers are learning to do more with less.

Computer Vision
Test-Time Baking Dramatically Speeds Novel View Synthesis

A new strategy learns to compress cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast high-fidelity novel-view rendering without reconstructing 3D geometry. This bridges the gap between decoder-only efficiency and ground-truth quality that previous test-time training methods sacrificed.

TTB achieves state-of-the-art view synthesis quality while reducing computational overhead compared to methods that reconstruct explicit 3D.
Lin, Hachiuma, Choe et al. 2611.17331 PDF
Computer Vision
Production-Ready Geometry Foundation Model Integrates Pose Optimization

Kosmo-GFM combines a geometry foundation model with pose optimization and real-world supervision from KosmoWorld to predict camera parameters, depth, correspondences, and 3D points from images and video. This enables downstream 3D/4D Gaussian splatting with scene-level geometric accuracy.

The system achieves production-grade scene reconstruction by closing the loop between foundation model predictions and geometric optimization, validated on real-world data.
Tang, Wei, Chen et al. 2611.16840 PDF
Machine Learning
Auditing AI Peer Reviewers with Injected Real Scientific Errors

Researchers created a benchmark that injects objective errors (mathematical, numerical, citation-based) into real papers and measures LLM reviewer detection rates. They also propose Skepthical, a multi-agent system that verifies claims by retrieving papers, using symbolic algebra, and executing code.

The first systematic evaluation of LLM-based peer review at production scale reveals significant gaps in current reviewer capabilities, especially for computational verification.
Zubeldia, Bolliet, Villaescusa-Navarro et al. 2611.17052 PDF
NLP
Smaller Clinical LLMs Learn to Be Concise via Length Control

Parameter-efficient fine-tuning typically produces verbose clinical reasoning in smaller language models, making outputs hard to act on in time-critical settings. This work introduces differentiable length control that constrains output conciseness without requiring preference optimization or reward models.

Small language models can match large proprietary models' reasoning quality while staying deployable on commodity hardware and respecting clinical time constraints.
Abbas, Malik, Qamar et al. 2611.17128 PDF

TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models

Decoder-only view synthesis models achieve high quality but are computationally expensive; this work proposes Test-Time Baking, which learns to compress global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP, enabling fast high-fidelity novel-view decoding without 3D reconstruction.

Video quality assessment typically requires complex multi-branch architectures; HiVE-VQA proposes the first JEPA-based video encoder for no-reference VQA, extracting hierarchical token features from a single frozen foundation model with minimal architectural complexity.

Multimodal language models bundle vision encoder design choices—upstream pretraining, dedicated capacity, and pre-fusion placement—making it hard to isolate individual effects; this work disentangles these choices empirically to understand what drives multimodal performance.

Featured Researcher
IZ
Íñigo Zubeldia
AI Evaluation Researcher · CMU/Max Planck Institute

Íñigo Zubeldia specializes in rigorous evaluation of AI systems, particularly LLM-based peer review and scientific output validation. His recent work on auditing AI reviewers brings much-needed empirical rigor to production-scale deployment of language models in high-stakes domains. Today's featured paper introduces the first systematic benchmark measuring LLM peer reviewer accuracy on real scientific errors, combining detection rates with novel multi-agent verification via symbolic computation—a vital step toward trustworthy AI in research.
